issues: Whether the termination clause limiting entitlements to ESA minimums is enforceable
Whether the 'for cause' provision in the termination clause is unenforceable for contracting out of the ESA standard for just cause
Whether the termination amounts to wrongful dismissal entitling the employee to common law reasonable notice
Whether termination shortly after return from medical leave gives rise to a claim of discrimination or reprisal based on disability under the Human Rights Code
Whether requiring execution of a release as a condition of receiving termination entitlements is lawful where statutory minimums are owed regardless
Whether the alleged policy breach constitutes just cause for dismissal at common law
What the appropriate common law reasonable notice period is given 14 years of service
Whether the termination clause is void in its entirety due to an unenforceable component (e.g., the for-cause provision) tainting the whole clause
key_facts: Employee had recently returned from medical leave prior to termination
Employment contract contained a termination clause limiting notice/severance to ESA minimums
Contract's for-cause provision purported to allow dismissal without notice for policy breaches
Employer required employee to sign a release to receive termination payments
causes_of_action: Wrongful dismissal (breach of contract / common law reasonable notice)
Human rights complaint - discrimination/reprisal on the basis of disability
Claim for unpaid ESA entitlements (termination and severance pay)
search_terms: for cause termination clause void contracting out ESA
disability discrimination termination after medical leave
wrongful dismissal common law notice factors
